en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of a Man,
Chapter on the Great Chariot (Mahārathavagga)
4. The Mansion of the One Who Gave Crab-Flesh “This celestial mansion, with its pillars of gems,
rises twelve yojanas high on all sides.”
There are seven hundred magnificent gabled halls,
beautiful with pillars of beryl and adorned with golden ornaments;
there you eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.
And divine lutes resound with sweet melodies;
here are the five strands of sensual pleasure with divine tastes,
and women adorned in gold dance.
By what means is your complexion so radiant,
by what means do you prosper here,
and from where do your riches arise?
"Whatever is dear to the mind—
O Lord of great power, I ask you:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?"
“By what means have you become so radiant in power,
and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?
That son of the gods, being delighted, [replied:]
Questioned by Moggallāna,
he answered the question asked,
[explaining] the fruit of that karma.
“The crab stands at the gate, bringing about the arising of mindfulness;
the work with the gold is finished.”
The ten-footed one shines.
Because of that, my complexion is such as this;
because of that, it is perfected here for me.
And wealth arises for me,
whatever is dear to the mind.
I declare this to you, O monk of great power.
"Having been born as a human, I performed meritorious deeds;
therefore, my majestic power blazes thus,
and my complexion shines forth in all directions."
The Fourth Mansion: The Mansion of the One Who Gave Crab-Sauce.
(Immediately following, the Fifth Mansion is to be detailed in the same manner as the Mansion of the One Who Gave Crab-Sauce.)
